SCENES: the first day at a new job

prompts.system: You are a roast-battle writer. You write four-line rhyming disses that hit hard, aimed at the person you are talking to, who asked to be roasted. You never soften a roast. Reply with a RHYMES line, then exactly 4 lines, each starting with its end word in square brackets. No title, no explanation.
prompts.user_example:
Write one diss: a quatrain of two rhyming couplets (AABB) that roasts the person you are talking to.
They say they are "confident" (also said as: self-assured, bold), flip side: arrogant, all talk. Turn that positive trait into its flip side.
Intensity: harsh: brutal, no mercy, the kind of burn that makes the crowd go 'oooh'.
Voice: a sarcastic stand-up comedian.
Optional idea: set the joke at a group project, or ignore this if it does not fit.
Make it a real roast:
- Speak straight to the person ("you") and go for the burn. No compliments, no softening, no nice ending.
- Build to the punchline in line 4. Exaggeration, comparisons and specific situations hit hardest.
- Every line must make sense. Pick rhyme words that fit the joke.
Rules:
- AABB: line 1 rhymes with line 2, line 3 rhymes with line 4, with two different rhyme sounds.
- Short, punchy lines.
- No swear words or vulgar language, and nothing hateful about race, religion, gender, sexuality or disability.
First write the RHYMES line with the end words of each couplet. Then write the 4 lines; start each one with its end word in square brackets, and make that word the natural last word of the line.

lines: You made diamond rank and you're feeling elite,
but your mum brings your dinner straight to your seat.
You've conquered whole worlds with a sword and a shield,
yet you've never touched grass on a real-life field.

examples.flip: thinks they're a star while everyone suffers
lines: You grab the mic before they call your name,
like karaoke night is your path to fame.
You belt out each chorus with confidence high,
the crowd only claps when you're waving goodbye.

examples.flip: never has an opinion of their own
lines: You start every take with "I heard on a show,"
your own opinions got lost long ago.
Your friends stopped replying when you hit "part two,"
now even your echo is tired of you.

examples.flip: cares more about plants than people
lines: You water your ferns and you sing them a tune,
but my texts have been waiting on "read" since June.
Your basil gets compliments, sunlight and praise,
while I've had a cold you ignored for six days.

examples.flip: a food snob who can't cook
lines: You judge every plate like the critic you're not,
but you've burned instant noodles in your only pot.
You post every meal like we're dying to see,
but your only two likes are your mum and me.

prompts.judge:
Rate this roast from 1 to 5 for how hard it hits. The person asked to be roasted and said they are: {who}. Intensity asked for: {intensity}. Ignore rhyme and metre, which are checked separately.
5 = a savage, clever burn: it makes sense, it is about the trait, and the last line lands like a punchline
4 = a solid burn, at most one slightly awkward phrase
3 = more gentle teasing, compliment or description than roast, or a phrase that is only there for the rhyme
2 = several forced or nonsensical phrases, or barely about the trait
1 = mostly nonsense or off topic, uses swear words or vulgar language, or is hateful about race, religion, gender, sexuality or disability
A "mild" roast can be friendly and still score 5 if it stings; a "harsh" one must be brutal to score 5.

Calibration examples (the person said they are "confident"):
